predecessors.name: Maya city-states (Preclassic and Classic)
predecessors.text: the northern and central lowlands kept in Cliopatria's 850 shape

successors.name: Spanish Empire
successors.text: the northern Yucatan Peninsula conquered in 1527-1546

successors.name: Itza kingdom of Nojpetén
successors.text: the Itza kingdom of the Peten, independent to 1697

ledger.x: 850: the Maya city-states continue in the north and the central lowlands after the southern kingdoms fall.
960: the central lowlands (Tikal, El Mirador, Uaxactun, Palenque) drop out.
1221: the seat of the northern Maya passes from Chichen Itza to Mayapan.
1450: the shape grows southward by about 201 cells to take in the central Peten (Tayasal), Zaculeu's country and Cozumel.
1525: Zaculeu, the Mam capital, falls to the Spanish.
1527: the first campaign of Francisco de Montejo lands on the east coast.
1529: about 49 cells of the southwest leave the shape.
1535: the Spanish are out of the peninsula but for Champotón.
1546: the last Maya resistance in the north is broken.
1546: the northern Yucatan passes to the Spanish.
1546: the last of the northern Maya provinces is conquered and the Postclassic Maya city-states end; only the Itza of the Peten remain free, to 1697.

wars.name: Spanish conquest of Yucatán
wars.outcome: Spanish victory after three attempts (1527-1528, 1531-1535, 1540-1546): permanent towns at Campeche and Merida in 1541-42, the Xiu of Mani allied with Spain, and the eastern provinces defeated in late 1546.

wars.name: Overthrow of Mayapan
wars.outcome: The Xiu revolted against the Cocom rulers of Mayapan; the Cocom were massacred and the city abandoned (1441 by written records, about 1461 by archaeology); the northern Yucatan broke into warring provinces.

certainty.note: No surveyed or treaty frontier: the shape is the envelope of the Puuc and Chichen Itza states, the Mayapan allies and the Yucatecan provinces; the Spanish towns of 1541-42 are points, not borders.
